images.name: 余烬·巨蟹
images.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: Skyrim fantasy weapon concept illustration for the Cancer zodiac (巨蟹座), part of an established geometric luminous bow collection. Create one polished portrait concept sheet, a complete large bow on the left occupying 70% of the canvas, and one enlarged matching grip detail on the right. The bow must be a credible single handheld bow with two balanced limbs, a slim taut string, and a continuous ergonomic palm grip; all tips visible. Cancer motifs abstracted as pincer arcs, armored shell segments, enclosing curves, NOT a literal crab sculpture. Entire weapon constructed from thick simple geometric solid-light bands and faceted translucent colored energy plates, substantial width and thickness, layered negative spaces, clear silhouette. No metal, wood, leather, gold fittings, realistic shell textures, six-pointed stars, giant magic circles, arrow, person, scene, watermark. Very dark charcoal studio backdrop. Controlled fluorescent colored edges, readable darker colored planes, restrained bloom never blowing out detail. A few local particles near limbs hint at the proposed draw effect, not a storm obscuring geometry. Buildable geometric design, no excessive tiny ornament. Exact Chinese title only, elegantly typeset at bottom: "余烬·巨蟹". Palette deep crimson, luminous scarlet, subtle rose-magenta accents. Design: bold angular twin pincer architecture. Two broad split sickle-like polygonal jaws above and below the palm curve toward the string but leave the arrow clearance open. Central grip is a beveled hourglass prism flanked by two open trapezoidal cages, distinct from any star or circular hub. Limbs made of five overlapping broad chevron shell plates per side, tapering strongly toward hooked angular tips, one continuous structural spine. Predominantly strong straight segments with controlled curved silhouette; aggressive, elegant. Particle proposal: a small trail of red triangular embers gathering along the inner pincer edges. Show complete bow and consistent enlarged grip detail. Portrait 2:3.
